Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 06-Feb-2025 (01:00 PM - 04:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.Tech. (CSE STREAM) EXAMINATION - FEBRUARY 2025  
  SUBJECT: MIE_1072 - BASIC MECHANICAL ENGINEERING SCIENCE  
  Basic Mechanical Engineering Science [MIE-1072]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  a  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               A superheated steam at 14bar is taken out from a boiler and is passed through a supply pipeline to (4)  
  a nearby industry for its use. The industry strictly requires 23.5% wet steam.  
  
  i) If the heat loss through the supply pipeline is 510kJ/kg, what is the temperature of superheated  
  steam at the boiler exit?  
  ii) If the heat loss in the supply pipeline is limited to 32.5% of latent heat of vaporization, what  
  should be the condition of steam at boiler exit in order to ensure that the 23.5% wet steam supplied  
  to the industry?  
  iii) If the thermal insulation on the supply pipeline is such that the steam does not lose any heat as it  
  passes through the supply pipeline, should the boiler still supply superheated steam?  
  
  Elaborate your answer. Assume the specific heat of water as 4.18 kJ/KgK and that of superheated  
  steam as 2.25 kJ/KgK..  
1B)               Three boilers supply steam into a common main. The pressure in the boilers and the main is 11.5    (3)  
  bar. Boiler-X which is equipped with a superheater produces 2500 grams of steam with a  
  temperature of 320°C. Boiler-Y is also equipped with a superheater and produces 13 kg of steam  
  with a temperature of 275°C. Boiler-Z does not have a superheater and it produces 3.5 kg of steam.  
  The temperature of steam in the mains is 232°C. Determine the quality of steam produced by  
  Boiler-Z.  
1C)               Explain the function of any three boiler accessories.                                                       (3)  
2A)               An 84mm wide belt transmitting power between two pulleys rotating in counter-clockwise directions (4)  
  with a speed reduction ratio of 9 has permissible tension per metre of the width as 11kN. The speed  
  and diameter of the larger pulley are 2.5rps and 1.6m respectively. Determine the power  
  transmitted by the drive and the length of the belt if the centre distance is 4meters and the  
  coefficient of friction between the belt and the pulley surface is 0.35. What would be the change in  
  length of the belt, if driven pulley rotation is changed to clockwise direction.  
2B)               The shaft from a DC motor is connected to gear A which rotates at 40rps in anti-clockwise direction. (3)  
  Gears B and C are compound gears as well as gears D and E. Gear A meshes with gear B and  
  gear C drives gear D. Gear E meshes with gear F which is mounted on the driven shaft. The  
  number of teeth on gears A, B, C, D, E and F are 27, 42, 55, 69, 75 & 88 respectively. Sketch the  
  arrangement and determine the speed (rpm) and direction of gear F? Calculate the centre  
  distance between the driver and driven shafts if the module of gears is 2π mm.  
2C)               Explain the function of fast and loose pulley with a neat sketch.                                           (3)  
3A)               A twin cylinder two-stroke petrol engine with bore to stroke ratio of 0.83, develops 70kW inside the        (4)  
  cylinder, that is running at 6500rpm. The mean effective pressure on the piston is 16 bar and  
  mechanical efficiency is 75%.  
  Determine the following:  
  i) Diameter and stroke of each cylinder  
  Page #1

ii) Brake thermal efficiency  
  iii) Indicated thermal efficiency  
  The fuel consumption is 16kg/hr of gross calorific value of 44MJ/kg.  
3B)   Explain the working of an engine fitted with a camshaft and operating on a thermodynamic cycle             (3)  
  wherein the heat addition and heat rejection takes place at isochoric processes. Support your  
  answer with neat sketches for each stage.  
3C)   Justify the following comments:                                                                            (3)  
  i) As compared with petrol engine, diesel engine is difficult to start in cold weather.  
  ii) Thermal efficiency is less in two-stroke engines.  
  iii) Number of working cycles per minute is equal to engine speed in two-stroke engines.  
4A)   Ozone friendly R134a is used in a refrigeration plant of 12 tonne capacity with evaporator and   (4)  
  condenser temperature of -10⁰C and 36⁰C respectively. Considering the condition of 6⁰C superheat  
  of the refrigerant at exit of the compressor.  
  i) Plot T-S and p-h for the cycle  
  ii) Calculate the mass flow rate of the refrigerant.  
  iii) Calculate the COP of the cycle.  
  iv) Calculate the condition and enthalpy of the vapor at the entrance to the evaporator.  
4B)   Discuss the functions of the following parts of a refrigeration system,                                    (3)  
  i) Expansion valve  
  ii) Evaporator  
  iii) Condenser  
4C)   Explain the following;                                                                                     (3)  
  i) In Vapor Compression Refrigeration Cycle (VCRS), why do the refrigerant is compressed before  
  entering the condenser?  
  ii) An ideal refrigerant should have higher specific heat in its vapor state, and lower specific heat in  
  its liquid state. Why?  
  iii) Does the latent heat of vaporization of the refrigerant effect the refrigerating effect produced?  
5A)   Differentiate between the following;                                                                       (4)  
  i) Conduction heat transfer vs Convection heat transfer.  
  ii) Open system vs Closed system.  
5B)   List out any six problems associated with NC machine.                                                      (3)  
5C)   Discuss the different components that make up an automated system for production system?                   (3)  
  Sketch a block diagram of the same.
